statusDefinitions.done: Implementation exists and has evidence; release/browser validation may still be pending.
statusDefinitions.in_progress: Work has started but implementation or verification remains.
statusDefinitions.planned: Not implemented yet, or no evidence is recorded.

milestones.title: Timeline model & version workflow
milestones.goal: Build a stable editing data model before expanding the visual editing workspace.

tasks.title: Timeline editing and Version management
tasks.summary: Master Timeline with visible typed layers, per-Shot active-Version dropdown (+ Add Version/Edit), nested Version timeline tabs, and separate master placement vs Version-internal timing.

subtasks.title: Switch a Shot/Slot active Version without changing other Slots
Create a new Version while preserving existing alternatives
Separate Master Shot placement/duration from Version internal timeline
Keep Master Timeline open and open nested Version timelines in tabs
Shot thumbnail dropdown with + Add Version and per-Version Edit action
Show typed layer lanes; remove generic Media track
Preserve nested versions/layers through Undo/Redo and project JSON

acceptance: Master Timeline remains accessible while Shot-Version timelines are open in separate tabs
Shot blocks display active-Version thumbnail or a clear placeholder and readable name
Version menu supports selecting an alternative, creating a new Version, and editing each Version
Master Shot placement/duration remains separate from its Version-internal timing
Project JSON preserves active Versions and nested layer/module relationships
Unit/integration tests and production build pass; no automated browser smoke test is added unless explicitly requested
evidence: Master Shot uses optional absolute masterStart with legacy sequential fallback; free placement snaps to frames, warns on overlaps, and Ripple Reorder packs the sequence without changing durations.
Master Timeline Video/Audio/Text/Procedural clip drag/drop is frame-snapped; moving a video keeps linked audio timing aligned.
The clip Inspector supports Split at midpoint, Split at playhead, and Duplicate clip. Video split/duplicate preserves linked audio, source offsets, fade boundaries and mix metadata.
Nested Version duration, module timing/source in/out, frame-snapped movement, explicit layer order, and compositor stacking order have regression coverage.

Trim operations synchronize sourceOut to the new duration and clamp fade values; JSON round-trip covers Master placement, nested layers, source ranges, linked audio, mute/mix settings, and saved thumbnail references.
CI run 39124022295: 93 tests pass across 10 files; TypeScript/production build pass; npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities.

PR #55 delivered frame-aligned clip-resize preview, grey overlap feedback, atomic adjacent-clip trimming with linked-audio/source-range updates, and cross-layer snap guides; CI passed 123 tests and TypeScript/Vite build.

PR #57 covers App-level resize/adjacent trim/Undo/Redo, cross-layer snapping, overlap prevention, nested Version history/export, and audio deletion/group-delete behavior. CI run 39165133176 passed 137 tests across 16 files plus TypeScript and production build at code/test SHA 794e3ff024c26d55d76583160d96238df8d84a12.

Follow-up correction for #53/#54: PR #55 did deploy, but user acceptance showed the nested clip UI still differed and drag snapping, cross-layer movement, and pointer-resize behavior were not fixed end to end. PR #57 replaces the drop placement logic, tracks resize via global pointer events, restores Master-style icon/thumbnail and two-line clip markup in nested timelines, and covers the interaction in App tests.
tasks.notes: Master and nested Version workflows, typed layers, Shot/Clip Version selection, separate Master vs internal timing, frame-snapped movement, split/duplicate, interactive resize preview, adjacent-trim-on-release, linked-audio/source-range propagation, and matching ruler/track/clip visuals are covered. PR #55’s first implementation deployed but missed acceptance for #53/#54; PR #57 corrects those gaps. Richer media preview/relink and missing-source recovery remain tracked under DYS-004/DYS-006; production MP4 export remains DYS-009.

tasks.title: Multi-track Timeline and linked audio
tasks.summary: Render video tracks as expandable groups with linked source-audio child lanes; unlink into independent Audio Layers with their own persistent mute controls.

subtasks.title: Validated video/audio clip model and source-audio links
Render linked audio as an indented child lane below its video layer
Unlink without changing current audio/video timing
Independent Audio Layer move/trim/delete after unlinking
Persistent per-audio-layer mute isolated from other layers
Undo/Redo and project JSON round-trip preserve links, mute, and track placement

acceptance: Expanding a video layer reveals linked source audio below it
Unlink converts the audio to an independent Audio Layer without moving or trimming either clip
Each audio layer has independent mute/unmute state
Deleting unlinked audio does not delete its video source
History and project JSON round-trip preserve link and mute state
Automated model/integration tests and build cover core behaviors; no automated browser smoke test unless explicitly requested
evidence: App integration tests cover linked child audio, per-clip mute, track-level mute, unlink and timing preservation.
Video split/duplicate operations preserve aligned linked audio, source offsets and audio mix metadata; unlink remains independently editable.
Audio track mute, clip mute, volume and fade settings are applied in playback/export and preserved by project JSON validation.
CI run 39124022295: 93 tests pass across 10 files; TypeScript/production build pass; npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities.

App integration coverage verifies independent audio edits after unlink, Undo/Redo for unlink/move/trim/delete, linked parent/child deletion, and preserving detached audio when a video layer is removed.
PR #57 CI run 39165133176 passed 137 tests across 16 files, TypeScript check, and Vite production build at code/test SHA 794e3ff024c26d55d76583160d96238df8d84a12.
tasks.notes: Linked-child lanes, unlink, independent audio move/trim/delete, track/clip mute, split/duplicate propagation, source-range/fade integrity, video-layer group-delete semantics, Undo/Redo, and project JSON coverage are implemented. Advanced automation/ducking/effects remain tracked under DYS-008 and are not part of this task.

tasks.title: Reusable Clip Assets and nested composition timeline
tasks.summary: Create reusable Clip Assets with editable, versioned nested timelines; pin versions in placements, prevent cyclic references, validate graph integrity, and render nested Clip compositions.

subtasks.title: Create Clip Assets with canvas dimensions and an initial empty Version
Open a Clip Version in its own Timeline tab and edit internal modules
Duplicate Clip Versions without mutating previous Versions
Pin Clip Version references and block direct or indirect cycles
Validate nested IDs, media references, frame geometry, and Code image references
Render nested Clip compositions and looped placements in the browser compositor
Add unit/integration coverage and production-build verification

acceptance: A Clip Asset can be created with a name, canvas width/height, and positive duration.
Each Clip Asset has one or more editable, independently versioned compositions.
A Clip Version can contain video, image, audio, text, Code/procedural, and nested Clip modules.
Nested Clip references pin a concrete Version and reject cycles.
Invalid or stale Clip, Version, Asset, and referenced-image IDs are rejected during project validation.
The compositor expands Clip placements recursively with the selected pinned Version and placement transforms.
Automated unit/integration tests pass and the production build succeeds.
evidence: Implementation and tests: PR #51
Workflow validation: https://github.com/ckfun0skf/dionysus-ai-video-editor/actions/runs/39153686513
Creative editing contract: public/doc/creative-editing-workflow-spec.md
Implementation details and known limits: public/doc/reports/reusable-clip-assets-report.md
tasks.notes: This status applies only to the reusable Clip Asset graph/nested-timeline slice. It does not claim production-grade frame-accurate MP4 export, complete Shot identity/version migration, or completion of the broader reference-management roadmap. Release/deployment remains tracked separately.

milestones.title: Preview, compositing & mobile editing
milestones.goal: Connect the editing model to a real preview rather than decorative controls.

tasks.title: Preview, playback, and media compositing
tasks.summary: Implement media playback and composition for Shot, Version, and master Timeline previews, including multi-layer picture-in-picture.

subtasks.title: Preview single imported media source
Composite multiple video/image layers in z-order
Canvas drag transform and Inspector synchronization
Contain/Cover/Stretch and background fill settings
Real first/last-frame thumbnails or explicit placeholders

acceptance: Master and nested Version tabs display a playhead-synchronized canvas preview with independent playhead state
Available image/video/text/nested composition layers render in stored z-order using their timing and supported transforms
Preview transform changes update the selected layer/clip/track geometry and persist with the project
Media fit and background settings are reflected in composition rendering
Missing/unreadable sources fail safely with visible fallbacks and clear recovery guidance
Automated tests and production build validate supported preview/composition behavior; no browser smoke test is required
evidence: src/App.tsx renders an integrated Master and per-Version canvas preview from the active composition at the current playhead; each Version tab retains its own playhead position.

src/compositionRenderer.ts resolves image/video sources, composites active layers in stored z-order, handles nested Clip assets, source in/out, contain/cover/fill, canvas geometry, backgrounds, border/opacity/animation, and supported audio volume/fades. Preview playback synchronizes source audio and updates video frames.
Existing tests cover per-tab preview/playhead, preview controls/project canvas settings, composition layer order and nested Clip version selection, plus normalized frame movement/resizing.
PR #57 adds a UI regression test proving a selected Video Layer's preview transform commits back to the layer model; test CI run 39165133176 previously passed 137 tests before this added case.
tasks.notes: The preview/compositor is implemented but still in progress: interactive preview scales to at most 1280×720, not a guaranteed 4K preview; browser codec/CORS/source availability still limits some media; durable media import/relinking is tracked under DYS-004; first/last-frame coverage is not uniform for every source. WebM export remains experimental and MP4 is tracked under DYS-009.

tasks.title: Advanced audio and procedural layers
tasks.summary: Support per-Audio-Layer mute/mixing, timed text, and first-class Three.js/procedural timeline layers with pinned script versions and explicit execution permission.

subtasks.title: Persist independent mute state for each Audio Layer
Multitrack audio level, trim, fades, and mixing

Pin script/module versions and isolate runtime errors

acceptance: Muting one audio layer does not mute any other layer and state persists
Three.js is represented as a typed procedural layer rather than a fake video asset
Saved Shot Versions pin exact script/module versions
Custom code executes only after explicit authorization in the defined security boundary
UI states clearly distinguish layer data, preview capability, and final render support
evidence: Independent track/clip mute and per-Audio-Layer volume, fade-in, and fade-out controls persist in Master and nested Version timelines.
Live playback and WebM export share the same normalized gain/fade envelope; WebM export schedules per-layer Web Audio gain curves.
Source in/out trim and split operations keep A/V relationships and source offsets consistent, clamp fade boundaries when durations change, and preserve JSON round-trips.
CI run 39124022295: 93 tests pass across 10 files; TypeScript/production build pass; npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities.
tasks.notes: Per-layer mute, volume/fades, source trim, linked A/V split, source-range preservation, fade clamping, and core JSON validation are implemented. Audio automation/ducking/effects, richer timed text, and safe/authorized procedural execution/rendering remain outstanding.
